note.p: One of Godwin's odder contacts. It looks as if the earliest contact is 1828 (although it is possible that the 1818 contact is also this person, since they meet in literary circless on that occasion). But we have taken the view that from 1828 Godwin is recognising a new individual - with whom he has only 'adv' contact and always at the theatre (and not usually the more distinguished or classical dramas). Spencer is noted alongside Skeffington and Barham, Hill and Lester Stanhope - and is clearly a theatre enthusiast. but we have yet to identify him. What is clear, is that these are all the same person! On June 14 1834, Godwin has the following entry, referring to a Lady (deleted) Mrs Spencer. 'Dine at Rickman’s, w. Frere, Dr Rigby Bunny, Paynes, Vardon, and lady(struck through), and mrs Spencer, and miss Seaton.@
